_meta.indication: Treatment of female adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kg with uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) caused by susceptible microorganisms: E. coli, K. pneumoniae, C. freundii complex, S. saprophyticus, and E. faecalis

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled randomized noninferiority study comparing oral gepotidacin 1500 mg to nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days
pivotal_trials.population: Female adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with uUTI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite response (combined subject-level clinical and microbiological response) at Test-of-Cure (TOC) in the micro-ITT nitrofurantoin-susceptible population
pivotal_trials.n: micro-ITT NTF-S population: 607 subjects (interim analysis; 320 gepotidacin, 287 nitrofurantoin)
pivotal_trials.result: Gepotidacin 162/320 (50.6%) noninferior to nitrofurantoin 135/287 (47.0%); treatment difference 4.3% (-3.6, 12.1); met prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3 randomized, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled (nitrofurantoin) noninferiority study; randomization 1:1
pivotal_trials.population: Female subjects greater than 12 years of age with uUTI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Composite response (combined clinical and microbiological response) at Test-of-Cure in the micro-ITT nitrofurantoin-susceptible population
pivotal_trials.n: micro-ITT NTF-S population: 541 subjects (interim analysis; 277 gepotidacin, 264 nitrofurantoin)
pivotal_trials.result: Gepotidacin 162/277 (58.5%) noninferior to nitrofurantoin 115/264 (43.6%); treatment difference 14.6% (6.4, 22.8); met prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (\ge1%): diarrhea (16% vs 3% nitrofurantoin), nausea (9% vs 4%), abdominal pain (4% vs 2%), flatulence (3%), headache (2%), soft feces (2%), dizziness (2%), vomiting (2%), and vulvovaginal candidiasis (1%). One serious adverse reaction of dysarthria attributed to gepotidacin; no deaths. Discontinuations for AEs 79/1,570 (5%) vs 30/1,558 (2%).
target_moa: Triazaacenaphthylene bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, thereby inhibiting DNA replication

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee was not held for this application.

description.text: Added new indication for uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea in patients 12 years and older weighing at least 45 kg with limited or no alternative options

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the addition of a new indication, use of Blujepa in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 45 kilograms (kg) who have limited or no alternative options for the treatment of uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea caused by susceptible strains of Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

basis.text: QIDP designation granted August 26, 2016 for uncomplicated urinary tract infections; a new QIDP designation granted January 8, 2019 following change to the gepotidacin mesylate salt tablet

citations.quote: uncomplicated urinary tract infections. QIDP designation was granted on August 26, 2016, for the requested indications.

On November 9, 2018, the Sponsor submitted a new QIDP designation request, due to a change in the product dosage form (b) (4) to a gepotidacin “mesylate salt” in a tablet. QIDP designation was granted on January 8, 2019, for the same indications granted on August 26, 2016.

summary.text: Gepotidacin (Blujepa) received approval via NDA 218230, a 505(b)(1) application submitted July 26, 2024. Substantial evidence of effectiveness was established with two or more adequate and well-controlled clinical investigations (the phase 3 noninferiority trials EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3). The product had QIDP designation (granted 2016 and re-granted 2019 for the mesylate salt tablet) and was granted priority review and filed September 24, 2024; no advisory committee was held.

citations.quote: On July 26, 2024, GlaxoSmithKline limited liability company (LLC), (the Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) new drug application (NDA) for gepotidacin 750 mg tablets, a triazaacenaphthylene bacterial type II topoisomerase inhibitor antibacterial drug intended to treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) in female adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older, weighing at least 40 k
Substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) was established with two or more adequate and well-controlled clinical investigations.
QIDP designation was granted on January 8, 2019, for the same indications granted on August 26, 2016.
The NDA was granted priority review status and was filed on September 24, 2024.
SEE was provided by data from two randomized, active-controlled phase 3 clinical studies in subjects with uUTI titled EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3.
